prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1436; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- The patient was treated for the same body area within the last two years, and that condition adds to the current complaints.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received from the claimant, who reports being stopped at a signal when a vehicle struck the rear of the insured car. The claimant is not represented by counsel and has asked for a copy of the claim file once it is open.

Entry 2: Confirmed that the driver is named on the policy and that the policy was active at the time of the collision. No issues with the policy terms were found.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report, which lists the claimant as an occupant of the vehicle at the scene. The responding officer's notes match the claimant's description of the impact.

Entry 4: Reviewed the photographs submitted by the claimant. They confirm the location of the damage and the general position of both vehicles, though they do not show the moment of impact. No independent witnesses have come forward.

Entry 5: Inspected the vehicle. The rear bumper, trunk lid, and tail light assembly damage is largely consistent with the described impact speed and direction. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known from prior claims or repair records.

Entry 6: Spoke with the claimant about reported neck and back strain. The claimant described the same account of the collision as in the initial report, with the same sequence of events and details.

Entry 7: Medical records show the claimant was treated for the same body area within the last two years. The prior condition appears to add to the current complaints, so the adjuster is noting it for the medical review.

Entry 8: Reviewed the injury against the kind and force of the collision. The reported symptoms fit well with the type of impact described and the damage to the vehicle.

Entry 9: Treatment followed a typical course of care. Visits and therapy sessions have tapered off as the claimant reports improvement in range of motion and pain levels.

Entry 10: Checked for any indication that the damage predates the start of coverage. Nothing in the file suggests that it does, and the policy effective dates fall well before the loss.

Entry 11: Reviewed the file summary. Liability appears clear on the basis of the police report and vehicle damage, and the claim is recommended to proceed to settlement review pending receipt of final treatment records.
